title: How this book works
lead: A London street cry: bakers sang it to sell hot spiced buns on Good Friday.
time_html:
Count 1 2 in every bar, steady as a clock: two beats a bar.

Walk on a beat; run two quick notes in one beat: say pen-ny, count 1 +.
pos:
Your hand. Right hand: finger 2 on middle C, 3 on D, 4 on E: the three middle fingers.

Steps down. E, D, C: each note is the next key down, and on the page each sits a step lower.
sing_how: Listen, pointing to each note. Sing it with the words, then on the letter names.
names_how: Now the notes are empty. Write E, D or C in each box, then sing it on the letter names.
more_how: The same three keys, a new way: a robot that walks with the band. Then make a tune of your own.
wow: Your first song with a band. Three notes, and you are already playing with drums and bass: scan the code, choose the band, and play on top. Then open your passport: Lesson 1 issues it.
trick: One note here is wrong. Play it, then the same bars on page 1: which note sounds wrong? Circle it.

yours.how: Pick one and play the whole song that way. Record it on a phone and listen back: does it sound the way you meant?
pick: Robot: every note short and stiff
Giant: slow and heavy, big footsteps

menu: As a giant, then a mouse
rhy_how: Say the words in time, then clap and count: clap on the coral numbers, hold through the grey ones.
label: Start here

gig.job: Welcome to Music Box 3. From this page on, no letters in the notes. You read them the way every pianist does: by where they sit on the five lines. The left hand stays in letters for a little longer.
gig.tool_how: Left hand. On C, play C; on G, play G. Once, on beat 1, and let it ring to the end of the bar.
gig.tool_cap: C then G (5, 1). F then C (2, 5). G then D (1, 4).
gig.song_how: Find your first note, then read by shape: next line or space up is the next key up; a jump on the page is a jump on the keys. Two landmarks: the curl of the clef wraps round the G line, and the middle line is B. A curved line joining two notes of the same height is a tie: play once and hold for both.
gig.real: Play it for someone younger. Count them in, 1 2 3 4, and do not stop.
gig.r_cap: 4 on G, 5 on A. Later the thumb slides up to D, then back to C.
gig.ready: you can start from any bar, not just the beginning.
ways_txt: Left hand: bottom key on beat 1, the top two keys on beat 3.
Play the tune eight keys lower. It sits near middle C and is easier to sing.

front:
Start here

Music Box 3

Eight songs and one old friend

Music Box 2 ended with one letter on the page. This book takes the last step, and then one more. First the notes stand with no letters at all, for both hands. Then the left hand disappears from the page, and you decide what it plays. That is the whole point of these three books.

Unit 2 · Real notes for the left hand too
4It’s a Long Way to TipperaryThe bass clef: chords as stacked notesWhole chords, read from notes
5We Three KingsSix counts; a minor homeTwo chords in a bar, read from notes
6John Brown’s BodyTwo shapes in every left-hand barLow note, then two notes, read from notes
Unit 3 · Only the tune and the chord names

The last page
Twinkle, YoursNothing but the tune and three namesYours to invent

The last page is Twinkle once more: the tune, three chord names, and nothing else. By then you will not need more.

Start here

How to use this book

For anyone learning without a teacher, and for teachers too

Finding a note without a letter
  • Right hand, the treble clef (the Queen). Her curl wraps round the second line from the bottom: that line is G.
  • Left hand, the bass clef (the King). His two dots sit either side of the second line from the top: that line is F.
  • Middle C sits on its own short line, just below the right-hand lines and just above the left-hand lines.
  • From any note you know, count: line, space, line, space. Each step is the next white key.
  • Do not count every note. Find the first one, then read the shape: up, down, step or jump.
  • ♯ and ♭ are written in front of every note they change, every time.
Fingers

This book prints no finger numbers. Choose your own and write them in pencil. Three rules cover almost everything: keep the hand in one place for as long as the tune allows; when it must move, move on a long note; going up, the thumb can tuck under, and going down, a finger can step over.

Two or three pages for every song

The first page gets you ready: the one new thing, the chords in the song with their keys, and five steps to practise in order. Then comes the song. Long songs run over two or three pages; the line that begins Ready for the next song when is always at the very end.

If you get stuck
  1. Play at half the speed. Then half of that.
  2. Take one line a day.
  3. In Unit 2, write the chord name over any left-hand shape you cannot read yet. Rub it out next week.
For teachers

Unit 3 is the destination of the series: a lead sheet, a table of chords and a menu of accompaniment patterns. The patterns are the ones taught, one at a time, across Music Box 1 and 2. Key signatures are not used yet; every accidental is written out.

Start here

Where the tunes come from

Every melody in this book is taken straight from an open score

In this book nothing was typed in by hand. Each tune, and the chord names above it, was converted by a program from a published open score, then checked back against that score note by note.
